answer_raw:
There isn't one single "best" city because different ranking organizations use different metrics, so the top spot depends entirely on whether you are measuring livability, economic power, or specific quality-of-life indicators.

## The Primary Rankings for 2026

**The EIU Global Liveability Index**
Published in July 2026, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) assesses 173 cities across five categories: stability, healthcare, education, culture/environment, and infrastructure [1][2]. This index focuses on how "comfortable" a city is to inhabit.
*   **Top Asian Cities:** **Osaka** ranked 7th and **Tokyo** ranked out of 173 at 10th as of July 2026 [1].
*   **Performance:** Both cities achieved perfect scores of 100 in stability, healthcare, and education [1].

**The Oxford Economics Global Cities Index**
This index evaluates 1,000 cities across economics, human capital, environment, and quality of life [4]. It is a broader look at global city dominance rather than just resident comfort.
*   **Top Quality of Life:** **Canberra** earned a perfect score of 100 for the "Quality of Life" category as of October 2026 [6].
*   **US Performance:** While **New York** took the No. 1 spot for the overall index as of October 2026, only one US city made the top 20 for the specific quality of life category [4].

**The Monocle Survey**
This ranking uses a qualitative approach, relying on correspondents to judge factors like connectivity, governance, and green space [5].
*   **Top City:** **Paris** took the top spot for quality of life as of June 2026, continuing a trend of European dominance [8].

## Comparison of Key Metrics

| Ranking Agency | Primary Focus | Top City / Leader | Key Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **EIU** (July 2026) | Resident comfort/livability | **Osaka** (7th) / **Tokyo** (10th) | Only Asian cities in the top 10 [1]. |
| **Oxford Economics** (Oct 2026) | Economic & human capital | **New York** (Overall) / **Canberra** (QoL) | Canberra led the specific QoL category [4][6]. |
| **Monocle** (June 2026) | Urbanism & connectivity | **Paris** | European cities have dominated recent years [8]. |
